newsitem.title: USA: Calif. senators seek reform to budget process.
newsitem.headline: Calif. senators seek reform to budget process.

text.p: Two California Senators introduced a measure Monday that would dock the pay of lawmakers when they are late enacting the state budget and make it easier for the legislature to pass the spending plan.

The Constitutional Amendment, introduced by Senate President Bill Lockyer and Senate Budget Committee Chairman Mike Thompson, would allow the state legislature to pass California's budget with a simple majority. A two-thirds vote of the legislature is required under current law.

The Constitutional Amendment would also require the budget to be signed into law no later than July 1, the start of the fiscal year. Only once in the last 10 years has the state had a budget by July 1.

"The failure to pass a timely budget impacts every taxpayer and business in our state," Thompson said. "The delays caused by this arbitrary two-thirds requirement have lowered our state's bond ratings, costing taxpayers upwards of $40 million a year in higher interest rates."
If approved by the legislature, the Constitutional Amendment would appear on the state ballot next year.
